jobs.title: Business Development Director
jobs.description:
At HDR, our employee-owners are fully engaged in creating a welcoming environment where each of us is valued and respected, a place where everyone is empowered to bring their authentic selves and novel ideas to work every day. As we foster a culture of inclusion throughout our company and within our communities, we constantly ask ourselves: What is our impact on the world?

Watch Our Story:' https://www.hdrinc.com/our-story'

Each and every role throughout our organization makes a difference in our ability to change the world for the better. Read further to learn how you could help make great things possible not only in your community, but around the world.

We believe architecture is more than designing buildings, it’s about providing solutions to societal challenges and creating stronger, more vibrant communities. As part of our Architecture practice at HDR, you’ll contribute to the design and delivery of spaces and experiences that advance community well-being around the world. From healing environments and learning spaces to research labs and civic landmarks and infrastructure, your work will directly influence how individuals experience the world around them. We bring together architects, planners, designers, and technical experts to solve complex design challenges with creativity, curiosity, and collaboration. From championing design excellence with an emphasis on resilience and sustainability to pioneering innovative building technologies, your contributions will leave a lasting impact on the built environment. This isn’t just a job, it’s a chance to drive meaningful change and help define the future of our communities.

We are in search of a Business Development Director to join our growing Civic + Justice Architecture practice and continue the legacy of providing our clients and communities with creative design solutions that improve the health and human condition of those they serve.

The primary responsibility of the Business Development Director is to grow and develop the civic architecture practice in the region. The successful candidate will focus on developing and winning new business relationships and opportunities with civic organizations and related institutions in the local and the regional market.

Business Development, Marketing and Practice Growth:

Experience in the local and regional Civic + Justice market to aid local Managing Principal in growing those practices
Collaboration with our national civic architecture leaders.
Create and support new or ongoing business opportunities for civic architecture practice.
Support HDR’s marketing and business development efforts to win business, including proposal strategy, proposal writing and interview presentations.
Elevate and represent the HDR brand across the region by attending conferences and other professional business events.
Bring energy, excitement and fun to a thriving practice.
Add value to the region to engage with the civic program strategically.

Client Management and Project Delivery Responsibilities:

Enjoy working directly with clients.
Direct client engagement and collaborate with project and regional leadership.
Prioritize efforts strategically to elevate the skillsets/needs of each office leader to identify client opportunities, pursuit specific requirements, and market awareness.
Capture Planning and Client Development Planning.
Cross mentoring Civic + Justice Principals and mentoring emerging leaders interested in client development, business development, and pursuit strategy.
Help keep our staff sharp, trained and effective for client development and interview requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in a related field
Maintain a professional registration or certificate
Civic + Justice experience in local and regional markets
Business development and client engagement in architecture industry in multiple geographies for multiple disciplines

Required Qualifications

A minimum of 15 years relevant industry experience
Demonstrated "self-starter" with a history of completing projects with limited oversight
Deep knowledge of the A/E/C industry's standard approach to procurement of professional services
Demonstrated ability to motivate and inspire others
Demonstrated ability to build a network of clients and industry partners
Experience in sales and developing effective win strategies
Strong financial acumen and negotiation skills
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Word, Excel and PowerPoint
Ability and desire to travel and engage with others in-person
Demonstrated experience in growing programs in new or highly competitive markets
Demonstrated experience in winning high-value contracts in the A/E/C industry
Demonstrated experience in writing compelling content based on information from technical staff

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

Our Commitment

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. Each group has an executive sponsor and is open to all employees.

We provide a comprehensive benefits package that promotes employee ownership, employee health, performance, and success, which includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, life insurance, an employee assistance program, paid time away, parental leave, paid holidays, a retirement savings plan with employer match, employee referral bonus and tuition reimbursement. The expected compensation range for this position depends upon skills, experience, education and geographical location. (Stated benefits are for full-time regular positions. jobs.company: ASU Foundation for a New American University
jobs.title: Executive Director of Advancement, West Coast
jobs.description:
Arizona State University Foundation has partnered with Lindauer, a national search and talent firm, to conduct this search. To apply, please submit your resume on the Lindauer website.

Please contact the Lindauer team leading this search if you have questions or would like to make a nomination or a referral: Adele Mezher, Senior Vice President and Emily Horsford, Senior Associate.

The salary range for this role is $180,000-230,000 annually.

The West Coast represents one of Arizona State University's most significant opportunities for philanthropic growth and broader engagement. ASU has built a growing presence through its academic programs, students and alumni, partnerships, physical locations, and connections to industries shaping the future. The opportunity now is to translate that presence into a more powerful and sustained culture of philanthropy in the region.

ASU Foundation seeks an entrepreneurial, strategic, and accomplished fundraising leader to serve as Executive Director of Advancement, West Coast. Based in California, the Executive Director will serve as a senior advancement leader for the region, building relationships with philanthropists, entrepreneurs, business and community leaders, alumni, and other partners whose interests intersect with the breadth and ambition of ASU.

The Executive Director will look beyond traditional sources of higher education philanthropy to identify new networks of wealth and influence. The region’s philanthropic landscape is not monolithic; success will require a leader who understands the distinct dynamics of the region including those between Northern and Southern California, recognizes where new wealth is emerging, and knows how to build authentic relationships within those communities.

This is both a frontline fundraising and leadership role. The Executive Director will personally cultivate, solicit, and steward a portfolio of significant donors and prospects while leading an experienced regional advancement team toward greater focus, collaboration, accountability, and philanthropic results. As momentum and philanthropic opportunity grow, the Executive Director will also have the opportunity to shape and expand the advancement operation to support ASU's ambitions across the region.

ASU brings an unusually broad set of assets to the West Coast, spanning health, science, education, technology, journalism, the arts and creative industries, Global Futures Laboratory, Thunderbird, and other areas of institutional strength. The Executive Director will translate those strengths into compelling philanthropic opportunities, connecting donor interests with the people, programs, and ideas capable of creating meaningful impact

For a creative and entrepreneurial advancement leader, this is an opportunity to help shape the next chapter of ASU's presence on the West Coast and build a culture of philanthropy matching the scale of the University's ambitions.

Reporting to the Chief Global Advancement Officer of the ASU Foundation, the Executive Director of Advancement, West Coast will lead ASUF's advancement strategy and regional team across California and the broader West Coast. The Executive Director will personally manage a significant portfolio of major and principal gift prospects while providing focused leadership, direction, and accountability to an experienced team.

Working across the ASU Foundation and in close partnership with university leadership, schools, colleges, institutes, the ASU Alumni Association, Sun Devil Athletics, and other ASU entities, the Executive Director will bring coordination and strategic focus to advancement activity across the region. The successful candidate will bring deep knowledge of the West Coast philanthropic and business landscape, strong executive judgment, and the ability to focus ASU's people and resources around the relationships and opportunities with the greatest philanthropic potential.

What You’ll Do

West Coast Advancement Strategy & Market Development

Design and lead a comprehensive advancement strategy for California and the broader West Coast, establishing priorities that advance ASU's institutional and philanthropic goals.
Build ASUF's philanthropic network across the region, identifying and engaging high-potential markets, emerging sources of wealth and influence, and individuals without an existing relationship to the University.
Apply knowledge of the region to differentiate among markets, identify where ASU has the strongest philanthropic opportunities, and focus institutional resources accordingly.
Develop a seamless and collaborative approach linking the ASU Foundation, ASU Alumni Association, Sun Devil Athletics, and other ASU units operating across the West Coast.

Principal & Major Gift Fundraising

Personally manage a significant portfolio of major and principal gift prospects, identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding high-net-worth individuals through sophisticated, multi-year strategies that raise donor sights and lead to seven-figure+ commitments.
Partner with constituent and central development officers, academic leaders, faculty, and other colleagues to connect donor interests with compelling opportunities across ASU.
Develop effective cultivation, solicitation, proposal, and stewardship strategies and ensure disciplined prospect management and tracking.
Meet ambitious personal and regional fundraising goals and provide timely reporting on progress, pipeline development, and solicitation results.

Team Leadership & Performance

Lead, coach, and develop an experienced West Coast advancement team, establishing clear priorities, expectations, accountability, and a shared focus on philanthropic results.
Help team members strengthen portfolios, elevate donor strategies, raise sights, and pursue increasingly significant opportunities.
Create an environment that encourages collaboration, initiative, sound judgment, and disciplined execution while providing directive leadership when needed.
Allocate team attention and resources toward the relationships, markets, and activities with the greatest potential to advance ASU's philanthropic goals.
Assess the structure and capacity of the West Coast advancement team over time, building the case for additional investment and thoughtfully growing the team.

University Partnership & Integration

Serve as a senior advancement partner and emissary for ASU across the West Coast, representing the University with credibility, enthusiasm, and intellectual depth.
Build trusted relationships with ASU leadership, including the President's Office, and work effectively across a highly entrepreneurial and decentralized university environment.
Navigate competing ideas and opportunities with discernment, determining where the Executive Director and team can add the greatest philanthropic value.
Bring together the right university leaders, faculty, programs, and advancement partners to connect donor interests and regional opportunities with ASU's institutional priorities.

What You'll Need

At least 10 years of successful development and related experience, preferably in higher education or another complex, mission-driven environment; bachelor's degree required and advanced degree preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Demonstrated success personally cultivating, soliciting, and closing seven-figure gifts; experience with larger principal or transformational gifts strongly valued.
Proven ability to raise donor sights, articulate ambitious ideas, and translate institutional priorities into compelling philanthropic opportunities.
Deep knowledge of California and the West Coast philanthropic and business landscape, with established relationships and networks and the credibility to build new ones.
Experience building relationships with high-net-worth individuals, entrepreneurs, business leaders, investors, and other sophisticated external constituents.
Demonstrated management experience, including the ability to lead experienced professionals, set direction, coach performance, and create accountability.
Sound judgment and demonstrated ability to establish priorities and maintain focus amid numerous initiatives, constituencies, and opportunities.
Intellectual curiosity, creativity, and entrepreneurial orientation, with the ability to understand opportunities across diverse academic, research, and programmatic areas and translate ideas and relationships into philanthropic results.
Highly collaborative style and demonstrated ability to build trust and work across organizational boundaries in a complex, decentralized environment.
Executive presence, maturity, integrity, discretion, and the ability to represent ASU effectively with senior institutional and external leaders.
Strong communication skills, including the ability to develop sophisticated proposals and related donor materials.
Working knowledge of Salesforce or comparable donor/prospect management systems and a commitment to disciplined moves management and reporting.
An advocate's belief in the vision of ASU as a New American University and enthusiasm for the University's Charter and mission.
Ability and willingness to travel frequently throughout the West Coast and to Arizona and to work a flexible schedule when required.

Benefits

Comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance
401(k) plan with matching employer contribution
Parental leave
22 days of vacation time
11 holidays, including your birthday
Cell phone reimbursement
Significant tuition reductions
Professional development is highly valued at ASU Enterprise Partners; employees are encouraged to look across the organization and nurture new areas of interest

About ASU Foundation

The ASU Foundation
fosters partnerships between ASU and like-minded individuals, corporations and foundations who believe in ASU’s mission and provide resources for ASU to manifest its charter into meaningful impact. These partnerships empower ASU to advance student access, serve our community, protect the planet, create equity in higher education and conduct research for the public good.

At the ASU Foundation we value

Character

We prioritize character and integrity in every decision and action, establishing trust as the foundation of all that we do.

Service

We are dedicated to serving our students, donors, communities, and colleagues by fostering support and collaboration to ensure that our efforts are impactful.

Innovation

Innovation drives us to create meaningful opportunities and solutions, helping every member of our global community achieve meaningful outcomes.

jobs.title: Director of Development
jobs.description:
Reporting to the Executive Director, the Director of Development coordinates fundraising initiatives, including major and planned giving, annual appeals, corporate sponsorships, special events, membership, and donor stewardship, to maximize the ICA’s short and long-term revenue growth. 

The Director of Development is responsible for developing and monitoring revenue forecasts for the operating budget and prepares reports for the Board and committees on fundraising initiatives, revenue projections, and financial forecasting. They work closely with the Executive Director to steward and cultivate the Board of Trustees, and to implement special campaigns for exhibitions, collections, programs, and endowment. 

The Director of Development also serves as the staff liaison to the Board’s Development committee and works closely with the committee to design and implement fundraising strategy for the ICA San José’s Annual Benefit & Art Auction, which raises more than 10% of the annual operating budget. This work is supported by the Development and Membership Coordinator, with whom the Director of Development will work closely with to supervise and co-create successful fundraising programs in support of the ICA’s Vision and Mission and aligned with a core set of Priorities. 

The role maintains a visible community presence and regularly participates in networking, including events on evenings and weekends. This is a Knight Foundation grant-funded position, with the possibility for extension, with the goal of building the consistent contributed revenue stream to sustain intended institutional growth. 

Duties and Responsibilities 

In coordination with the Executive Director and Board President, manages and stewards Trustee giving. Supports the Executive Director and Nominating and Governance Committee to identify, cultivate, and recruit new Board members and other leadership volunteers, building their capacity to strengthen philanthropic relationships.
Supports solicitations by the Executive Director, preparing background information and helping develop strategies. Leads an active schedule of personal solicitations, cultivation visits/events, and stewardship activities, tracking this activity in the donor database. 
Develops a Board fundraising engagement plan, including expectations, training, and accountability structures for Trustee participation in solicitation and cultivation. 
Develops tailored cultivation and solicitation strategies for a portfolio of major prospects and donors; creates and presents written and oral proposals, especially framing long-time practices and new initiatives in compelling language, including development of an overall ICA case for support. 
Serves as a primary point person for Development events, coordinating event logistics, and communications while working closely with Board leadership and ICA staff. Occasional evening and weekend work for events and donor cultivation, etc. required. 
Builds upon the established moves-management system for tracking prospect stages, solicitation activity, and stewardship, with an eye towards eventual implementation of a robust CRM. 
Delivers regular reports to the Board of Trustees, Executive Committee, Development Committee, and Finance and Policy Committee on fundraising initiatives, revenue projections, and financial forecasts. 
Oversees the Museum’s signature annual Benefit & Art Auction, working closely with co-chairs, a committee, and ICA staff. 
Develops and executes strategies to maximize corporate funding opportunities, including matching gifts, sponsorships, and direct giving. 
Overhaul and oversee the current Membership program, creating new avenues for engagement and participation with the goal of seeing increased renewals.

Education and/or Experience: Bachelor's degree (B.A.) from a four-year college or university preferred, and five (5) years related experience and/or training, or equivalent combination of education and experience, including experience working with leadership donors, direct solicitations, and working with and coaching Trustees and leadership volunteers to conduct personal solicitations of these donors. 
Extensive knowledge of fundraising principles and strategies that span multi-year individual giving, corporate donations, membership, annual appeals, planned giving and events.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
About Trexquant
Trexquant is a systematic investment firm focused on building the research and trading infrastructure required to discover and deploy quantitative strategies across global markets.
Our mission is to build a platform that enables researchers to backtest and implement almost any type of cross-region and cross-asset alpha idea. We want researchers to be able to move efficiently from an investment hypothesis to simulation, evaluation, and ultimately production trading.
Achieving this requires much more than building a backtester. It requires an integrated research and trading platform that supports multiple asset classes, regions, data sources, execution venues, brokers, and counterparties.
The Role
We are seeking a Chief Operating Officer who can turn this vision into an executable plan and ensure that the organization delivers on it.
The COO will work closely with the CEO and leaders across research, engineering, trading, data, operations, and other functions to establish clear goals, assign ownership, identify dependencies, and drive projects through completion.
This is a highly execution-oriented role. We are looking for someone who can take ambitious, sometimes loosely defined objectives and translate them into concrete projects with measurable milestones and accountable owners.
Key Responsibilities
Translate Trexquant's strategic vision into clear, measurable company-wide goals and execution plans
Drive the development of a unified research and trading platform capable of supporting cross-region and cross-asset quantitative strategies
Coordinate research, engineering, data, trading, execution, and operational teams to ensure that the necessary infrastructure is delivered
Establish priorities, milestones, ownership, and timelines for major initiatives and continuously track progress against them
Identify bottlenecks and dependencies that prevent researchers from moving efficiently from an idea to backtest to production
Help expand the firm's capabilities across equities, futures, corporate bonds, options, ETFs, FX, and other asset classes
Coordinate the operational infrastructure required to trade across multiple markets, brokers, counterparties, and execution venues
Develop scalable processes that allow the organization to continue executing effectively as the firm grows
Hold teams accountable for results while helping remove organizational and technical obstacles
Continuously look for opportunities to automate processes and use AI to make research, engineering, trading, and operations more efficient

Requirements

What We Are Looking For
The ideal candidate is an exceptional operator who combines strategic thinking with a strong bias toward execution.
You should be comfortable working across highly technical teams and understanding complex systems well enough to identify the important problems, ask the right questions, establish priorities, and ensure that they are solved.
We value candidates who{{:}}
Have demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional organizations or initiatives
Are exceptionally strong at setting goals and driving execution
Can break large, ambiguous problems into concrete and manageable projects
Understand technology and quantitative systems sufficiently to work effectively with researchers and engineers
Can coordinate many simultaneous initiatives without losing sight of the firm's larger objectives
Create accountability through clear ownership and measurable outcomes
Are intellectually curious and willing to learn unfamiliar areas quickly
Are comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where priorities evolve as new opportunities emerge

What Success Looks Like
Success in this role means steadily removing the barriers between a researcher's idea and its implementation.
Over time, a Trexquant researcher should be able to formulate a cross-asset or cross-region investment hypothesis, access the necessary data, backtest it accurately, evaluate it, and deploy it to production through a common platform with increasingly little manual infrastructure work.
The COO's responsibility is to help organize and drive the company toward making that vision a reality.

Benefits

Competitive salary with performance-based bonus
Collaborative, casual, and friendly work environment
PPO health, dental, and vision insurance fully covered for you and your dependents
Pre-tax commuter benefits
Weekly company-provided meals

The base salary range is $200,000 to $300,000, depending on candidates' educational and professional background. Base salary is only one part of Trexquant's total compensation, which may include a discretionary and performance based bonus.

Trexquant is an Equal Opportunity Employer

Read this first

This is an operator seat. We are not hiring a nurse manager, a “people person,” or someone whose value is chatting with patients in the lobby. The last hire at that profile failed. The next hire will be judged on whether staff can run the same process without the owner, whether the EMR and RCM actually work, and whether training sticks.
If your background is floor nursing, charge nurse, or clinical supervisor and you have not built computer workflows yourself, do not apply.

Compensation — South Mississippi
We are paying above the local administrator market on purpose to attract a builder with an IT / systems background.
* Base salary: $160,000 – $185,000
* Target total cash: $175,000 – $200,000 (base + performance bonus)
* Bonus earned on: days in A/R, clean-claim / denial rate, collections vs charges, written SOPs in use at all three sites, and documented staff competency — not  friendliness and not raw visit volume

* Relocation considered if the candidate will live within a workable drive of the three sites
This pay is for a person who can design the internal operating system of the practice. It is not available to a recycled clinic manager.

What you will build
* The practice operating system: one written workflow for intake, insurance verification, authorization, scheduling, procedure day, coding, claim, denial, and collection — identical at all three offices
* The computer layer: EMR/RCM (CureMD or successor), Google Workspace, phones, scanners, e-fax, ultrasound/device workflows, portal, and any automation. You configure it. You train staff on it. You own the tickets
* A training program: checklists, competency sign-off, and retraining when someone drifts. “I told them” is not training
* A weekly scorecard the owner can read in ten minutes: volume, procedures, collections, A/R aging, denials, no-shows, open tickets
* Multi-site discipline: inventory, equipment, coverage, policies, and support for facility expansion
* Vendors and IT: you speak to them, you do not escalate every login to the physician

Required background
* IT or systems experience that is real: EMR administration, practice-management software, workflow automation, reporting, or healthcare IT — not “I’m comfortable with computers”
* You have personally built templates, work queues, charge tickets, and staff training inside an EMR/RCM. Be ready to screen-share and show how
* 5+ years running operations in an outpatient specialty setting (vein/vascular, derm, plastics, ortho, pain, urology, GI, OBL, or similar). Multi-site required or strongly preferred
* Proven staff trainer: you have written SOPs and can point to people who still follow them after you left the room
* Direct communicator. Travels Hattiesburg, the Coast, and Meridian without being asked twice
* Nice to have: MHA, MBA, or equivalent only if paired with hands-on systems work. A degree without a build record does not qualify.

Disqualifiers — do not apply if
* Your last role was nurse manager, charge nurse, or clinical supervisor and operations meant “keeping the floor calm”
* You describe your strength as patient rapport, bedside manner, or being the face of the office
* You need the physician or a vendor to fix EMR, claims, or report problems
* You have never written a workflow or trained a team to a documented standard
* You want a CEO title and strategy meetings more than you want queues, denials, and SOPs

How we will hire (this is the filter)

* 90-minute working session, not a personality interview: open a denial/aging report, map one broken workflow, and write the first page of the fix
* Live EMR or analogous systems exercise. If you cannot navigate a practice system, the process ends

* References must include a physician-owner and at least one employee you trained — not only peers who liked you
* 90-day scorecard will be written into the offer: SOPs live at all three sites, staff competency documented, A/R and denial movement, owner time out of daily firefighting. Miss the build, and the seat does not continue.

How to apply

Email a résumé and a one-page note with exactly four items : (1) EMR/RCM/IT systems you configured yourself, (2) sites and headcount you ran, (3) one workflow you built and the metric that moved, (4) how you train staff when they do not follow the process. Advertising Copy

The Opportunity

The University of Vermont (UVM) invites nominations and applications for the position of Executive Director of Institutional Research and Assessment. Reporting to the Provost, the Executive Director will provide enterprise-level leadership for the Office of Institutional Research and Assessment (OIRA), advancing a strategic data, assessment, and decision-support agenda that strengthens institutional effectiveness, informs executive decision-making, and supports the University’s mission. This leader will foster a culture of responsible, transparent, and actionable data use; align data governance, analytics, assessment, and emerging technologies with institutional goals; and serve as a trusted advisor on the interpretation and strategic application of institutional data. The next Executive Director will also help define OIRA’s future role as both a steward of UVM’s official institutional data and a strategic partner with leaders across the University.

OIRA is responsible for the use and reporting of the University’s official institutional data and statistics regarding students, faculty, and staff, including accreditation, IPEDS reporting, and college ranking data, to name a few. The next Executive Director will provide institutional leadership, in partnership with Enterprise Technology Services, for data governance, stewardship, and architecture to ensure secure, accurate, reliable, and accessible data that supports regulatory reporting, contractual obligations, external requirements, institutional accountability, and lifecycle management practices that ensure data is collected, maintained, used, and retained in ways that are purposeful, efficient, and sustainable. They will work to advance an enterprise business intelligence and analytics strategy, including institutional metrics, dashboards, and self-service capabilities, while building campus-wide capacity for data- informed decision-making, data literacy, privacy and security, and the responsible and ethical use of advanced analytics and artificial intelligence, and lead adoption of these tools and practices across units to ensure consistent and effective use.

UVM is composed of nine schools and colleges, including the nationally recognized Larner College of Medicine, and offers a broad array of undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs. UVM enrolls approximately 14,000 students, including undergraduate, graduate, and medical students, across a variety of teaching modalities, and is supported by more than 4,000 faculty and staff. The University of Vermont is a public land-grant R1 research university, and is consistently recognized for its leadership in sustainability, inclusive excellence, and student

engagement, and has been ranked among the nation’s top public universities for making an impact. The schools and colleges offer over 100 bachelor’s degrees and more than 120 graduate degrees and certificate programs. To learn more about UVM, please visit: https://www.uvm.edu/

Providing Support and Direction to a Strong Team

The OIRA office has a team of analysts and assessment professionals who are deeply committed to meeting the needs of the University. The next Executive Director will have the opportunity to build on this strong foundation by clarifying priorities, strengthening internal alignment, developing a sustainable service model, and positioning the team as a responsive, trusted, and strategic partner to academic and administrative units across UVM. In partnership with colleagues from Enterprise Technology Services, the Executive Director will also provide leadership for the data governance and data stewardship structures of UVM.

Providing Institutional Data and Analytics to Undergird the Implementation of the New Strategic Plan

As President Tromp establishes the University’s strategic direction through the finalization of the new strategic plan, Green, Gold, and Bold

The identification, definition and tracking of institution-wide metrics of achievement, and the distribution across the institution of responsibilities for achieving these metrics will be a first priority. OIRA will also support individual units, both in identifying and tracking their contributions to the institution-wide metrics outlined in the strategic plan, and for metrics specific to their divisional and unit goals. In this work, the Executive Director will have the opportunity to work closely with a variety of leaders across the campus in defining measures, identifying data sources, and then providing regular and timely reporting on the progress toward strategic objectives.

Support for Accreditation Analysis and Reporting

As a large public land-grant research university with an affiliated major medical center, UVM has significant institutional, programmatic, accreditation, financial aid, IPEDS, ranking, and external reporting obligations. The different programs, schools and colleges look to OIRA to assist with identification of key data needed for accrediting purposes, as well as retrieving, analyzing, and formatting the data elements to meet accreditation requirements. While OIRA has a strong reputation for excellence in this work, the new Executive Director will have the opportunity to further enhance the office’s approach, and where appropriate, formalize and standardize processes to support accreditation reporting across the institution.

Using Key Institutional Data to Provide Future Projections of Key Policy Areas and Make Policy Recommendations

As institutional data becomes increasingly integrated throughout the institution, and the use of AI becomes ever more ubiquitous, the need for sophisticated analysis and the ability for university leadership to utilize the analysis quickly and effectively becomes even more important. The next Executive Director has the opportunity to shape the future of UVM’s data use, working closely with stakeholders such as members of the senior leadership team, Deans, and other campus leaders, as well as with key offices that support access in a variety of ways. As the University advances a phased approach to ERP readiness and broader enterprise systems planning, the Executive Director will play an important role in aligning institutional data, analytics, reporting, and governance capabilities with evolving institutional needs. The Executive Director will have the opportunity to enhance existing relationships, build new ones, and advance a more comprehensive institutional view of UVM with this broader institutional picture. The next leader should be a proactive partner across the institution who only facilitates ease of access to an ever-growing data set, but who also provides strategic advice and insights about institutional/departmental efficiencies, makes policy recommendations, and supports future planning and projections.

Founded in 1791 as the fifth college in New England, the University of Vermont is one of the nation’s oldest universities, and among its most distinctive. new_jobs.description:
Arizona State University Foundation has partnered with Lindauer, a national search and talent firm, to conduct this search. To apply, please submit your resume on the Lindauer website.

Please contact the Lindauer team leading this search if you have questions or would like to make a nomination or a referral: Adele Mezher, Senior Vice President and Emily Horsford, Senior Associate.

The salary range for this role is $180,000-230,000 annually.

The West Coast represents one of Arizona State University's most significant opportunities for philanthropic growth and broader engagement. ASU has built a growing presence through its academic programs, students and alumni, partnerships, physical locations, and connections to industries shaping the future. The opportunity now is to translate that presence into a more powerful and sustained culture of philanthropy in the region.

ASU Foundation seeks an entrepreneurial, strategic, and accomplished fundraising leader to serve as Executive Director of Advancement, West Coast. Based in California, the Executive Director will serve as a senior advancement leader for the region, building relationships with philanthropists, entrepreneurs, business and community leaders, alumni, and other partners whose interests intersect with the breadth and ambition of ASU.

The Executive Director will look beyond traditional sources of higher education philanthropy to identify new networks of wealth and influence. The region’s philanthropic landscape is not monolithic; success will require a leader who understands the distinct dynamics of the region including those between Northern and Southern California, recognizes where new wealth is emerging, and knows how to build authentic relationships within those communities.

This is both a frontline fundraising and leadership role. The Executive Director will personally cultivate, solicit, and steward a portfolio of significant donors and prospects while leading an experienced regional advancement team toward greater focus, collaboration, accountability, and philanthropic results. As momentum and philanthropic opportunity grow, the Executive Director will also have the opportunity to shape and expand the advancement operation to support ASU's ambitions across the region.

ASU brings an unusually broad set of assets to the West Coast, spanning health, science, education, technology, journalism, the arts and creative industries, Global Futures Laboratory, Thunderbird, and other areas of institutional strength. The Executive Director will translate those strengths into compelling philanthropic opportunities, connecting donor interests with the people, programs, and ideas capable of creating meaningful impact

For a creative and entrepreneurial advancement leader, this is an opportunity to help shape the next chapter of ASU's presence on the West Coast and build a culture of philanthropy matching the scale of the University's ambitions.

Reporting to the Chief Global Advancement Officer of the ASU Foundation, the Executive Director of Advancement, West Coast will lead ASUF's advancement strategy and regional team across California and the broader West Coast. The Executive Director will personally manage a significant portfolio of major and principal gift prospects while providing focused leadership, direction, and accountability to an experienced team.

Working across the ASU Foundation and in close partnership with university leadership, schools, colleges, institutes, the ASU Alumni Association, Sun Devil Athletics, and other ASU entities, the Executive Director will bring coordination and strategic focus to advancement activity across the region. The successful candidate will bring deep knowledge of the West Coast philanthropic and business landscape, strong executive judgment, and the ability to focus ASU's people and resources around the relationships and opportunities with the greatest philanthropic potential.

What You’ll Do

West Coast Advancement Strategy & Market Development

Design and lead a comprehensive advancement strategy for California and the broader West Coast, establishing priorities that advance ASU's institutional and philanthropic goals.
Build ASUF's philanthropic network across the region, identifying and engaging high-potential markets, emerging sources of wealth and influence, and individuals without an existing relationship to the University.
Apply knowledge of the region to differentiate among markets, identify where ASU has the strongest philanthropic opportunities, and focus institutional resources accordingly.
Develop a seamless and collaborative approach linking the ASU Foundation, ASU Alumni Association, Sun Devil Athletics, and other ASU units operating across the West Coast.

Principal & Major Gift Fundraising

Personally manage a significant portfolio of major and principal gift prospects, identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding high-net-worth individuals through sophisticated, multi-year strategies that raise donor sights and lead to seven-figure+ commitments.
Partner with constituent and central development officers, academic leaders, faculty, and other colleagues to connect donor interests with compelling opportunities across ASU.
Develop effective cultivation, solicitation, proposal, and stewardship strategies and ensure disciplined prospect management and tracking.
Meet ambitious personal and regional fundraising goals and provide timely reporting on progress, pipeline development, and solicitation results.

Team Leadership & Performance

Lead, coach, and develop an experienced West Coast advancement team, establishing clear priorities, expectations, accountability, and a shared focus on philanthropic results.
Help team members strengthen portfolios, elevate donor strategies, raise sights, and pursue increasingly significant opportunities.
Create an environment that encourages collaboration, initiative, sound judgment, and disciplined execution while providing directive leadership when needed.
Allocate team attention and resources toward the relationships, markets, and activities with the greatest potential to advance ASU's philanthropic goals.
Assess the structure and capacity of the West Coast advancement team over time, building the case for additional investment and thoughtfully growing the team.

University Partnership & Integration

Serve as a senior advancement partner and emissary for ASU across the West Coast, representing the University with credibility, enthusiasm, and intellectual depth.
Build trusted relationships with ASU leadership, including the President's Office, and work effectively across a highly entrepreneurial and decentralized university environment.
Navigate competing ideas and opportunities with discernment, determining where the Executive Director and team can add the greatest philanthropic value.
Bring together the right university leaders, faculty, programs, and advancement partners to connect donor interests and regional opportunities with ASU's institutional priorities.

What You'll Need

At least 10 years of successful development and related experience, preferably in higher education or another complex, mission-driven environment; bachelor's degree required and advanced degree preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Demonstrated success personally cultivating, soliciting, and closing seven-figure gifts; experience with larger principal or transformational gifts strongly valued.
Proven ability to raise donor sights, articulate ambitious ideas, and translate institutional priorities into compelling philanthropic opportunities.
Deep knowledge of California and the West Coast philanthropic and business landscape, with established relationships and networks and the credibility to build new ones.
Experience building relationships with high-net-worth individuals, entrepreneurs, business leaders, investors, and other sophisticated external constituents.
Demonstrated management experience, including the ability to lead experienced professionals, set direction, coach performance, and create accountability.
Sound judgment and demonstrated ability to establish priorities and maintain focus amid numerous initiatives, constituencies, and opportunities.
Intellectual curiosity, creativity, and entrepreneurial orientation, with the ability to understand opportunities across diverse academic, research, and programmatic areas and translate ideas and relationships into philanthropic results.
Highly collaborative style and demonstrated ability to build trust and work across organizational boundaries in a complex, decentralized environment.
Executive presence, maturity, integrity, discretion, and the ability to represent ASU effectively with senior institutional and external leaders.
Strong communication skills, including the ability to develop sophisticated proposals and related donor materials.
Working knowledge of Salesforce or comparable donor/prospect management systems and a commitment to disciplined moves management and reporting.
An advocate's belief in the vision of ASU as a New American University and enthusiasm for the University's Charter and mission.
Ability and willingness to travel frequently throughout the West Coast and to Arizona and to work a flexible schedule when required.

Benefits

Comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance
401(k) plan with matching employer contribution
Parental leave
22 days of vacation time
11 holidays, including your birthday
Cell phone reimbursement
Significant tuition reductions
Professional development is highly valued at ASU Enterprise Partners; employees are encouraged to look across the organization and nurture new areas of interest

About ASU Foundation

The ASU Foundation
fosters partnerships between ASU and like-minded individuals, corporations and foundations who believe in ASU’s mission and provide resources for ASU to manifest its charter into meaningful impact. These partnerships empower ASU to advance student access, serve our community, protect the planet, create equity in higher education and conduct research for the public good.

At the ASU Foundation we value

Character

We prioritize character and integrity in every decision and action, establishing trust as the foundation of all that we do.

Service

We are dedicated to serving our students, donors, communities, and colleagues by fostering support and collaboration to ensure that our efforts are impactful.

Innovation

Innovation drives us to create meaningful opportunities and solutions, helping every member of our global community achieve meaningful outcomes.

About Trexquant
Trexquant is a systematic investment firm focused on building the research and trading infrastructure required to discover and deploy quantitative strategies across global markets.
Our mission is to build a platform that enables researchers to backtest and implement almost any type of cross-region and cross-asset alpha idea. We want researchers to be able to move efficiently from an investment hypothesis to simulation, evaluation, and ultimately production trading.
Achieving this requires much more than building a backtester. It requires an integrated research and trading platform that supports multiple asset classes, regions, data sources, execution venues, brokers, and counterparties.
The Role
We are seeking a Chief Operating Officer who can turn this vision into an executable plan and ensure that the organization delivers on it.
The COO will work closely with the CEO and leaders across research, engineering, trading, data, operations, and other functions to establish clear goals, assign ownership, identify dependencies, and drive projects through completion.
This is a highly execution-oriented role. We are looking for someone who can take ambitious, sometimes loosely defined objectives and translate them into concrete projects with measurable milestones and accountable owners.
Key Responsibilities
Translate Trexquant's strategic vision into clear, measurable company-wide goals and execution plans
Drive the development of a unified research and trading platform capable of supporting cross-region and cross-asset quantitative strategies
Coordinate research, engineering, data, trading, execution, and operational teams to ensure that the necessary infrastructure is delivered
Establish priorities, milestones, ownership, and timelines for major initiatives and continuously track progress against them
Identify bottlenecks and dependencies that prevent researchers from moving efficiently from an idea to backtest to production
Help expand the firm's capabilities across equities, futures, corporate bonds, options, ETFs, FX, and other asset classes
Coordinate the operational infrastructure required to trade across multiple markets, brokers, counterparties, and execution venues
Develop scalable processes that allow the organization to continue executing effectively as the firm grows
Hold teams accountable for results while helping remove organizational and technical obstacles
Continuously look for opportunities to automate processes and use AI to make research, engineering, trading, and operations more efficient

Requirements

What We Are Looking For
The ideal candidate is an exceptional operator who combines strategic thinking with a strong bias toward execution.
You should be comfortable working across highly technical teams and understanding complex systems well enough to identify the important problems, ask the right questions, establish priorities, and ensure that they are solved.
We value candidates who{{:}}
Have demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional organizations or initiatives
Are exceptionally strong at setting goals and driving execution
Can break large, ambiguous problems into concrete and manageable projects
Understand technology and quantitative systems sufficiently to work effectively with researchers and engineers
Can coordinate many simultaneous initiatives without losing sight of the firm's larger objectives
Create accountability through clear ownership and measurable outcomes
Are intellectually curious and willing to learn unfamiliar areas quickly
Are comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where priorities evolve as new opportunities emerge

Read this first

This is an operator seat. We are not hiring a nurse manager, a “people person,” or someone whose value is chatting with patients in the lobby. The last hire at that profile failed. The next hire will be judged on whether staff can run the same process without the owner, whether the EMR and RCM actually work, and whether training sticks.
If your background is floor nursing, charge nurse, or clinical supervisor and you have not built computer workflows yourself, do not apply.

Compensation — South Mississippi
We are paying above the local administrator market on purpose to attract a builder with an IT / systems background.
* Base salary: $160,000 – $185,000
* Target total cash: $175,000 – $200,000 (base + performance bonus)
* Bonus earned on: days in A/R, clean-claim / denial rate, collections vs charges, written SOPs in use at all three sites, and documented staff competency — not  friendliness and not raw visit volume
* Benefits: health, dental, vision; 401(k) with match; PTO-120 hours and 5 sick days; travel allowance for travel between offices; professional development allowance; practice-issued laptop and mobile phone
* Relocation considered if the candidate will live within a workable drive of the three sites
This pay is for a person who can design the internal operating system of the practice. It is not available to a recycled clinic manager.

What you will build
* The practice operating system: one written workflow for intake, insurance verification, authorization, scheduling, procedure day, coding, claim, denial, and collection — identical at all three offices
* The computer layer: EMR/RCM (CureMD or successor), Google Workspace, phones, scanners, e-fax, ultrasound/device workflows, portal, and any automation. You configure it. You train staff on it. You own the tickets
* A training program: checklists, competency sign-off, and retraining when someone drifts. “I told them” is not training
* A weekly scorecard the owner can read in ten minutes: volume, procedures, collections, A/R aging, denials, no-shows, open tickets
* Multi-site discipline: inventory, equipment, coverage, policies, and support for facility expansion
* Vendors and IT: you speak to them, you do not escalate every login to the physician

Required background
* IT or systems experience that is real: EMR administration, practice-management software, workflow automation, reporting, or healthcare IT — not “I’m comfortable with computers”
* You have personally built templates, work queues, charge tickets, and staff training inside an EMR/RCM. Be ready to screen-share and show how
* 5+ years running operations in an outpatient specialty setting (vein/vascular, derm, plastics, ortho, pain, urology, GI, OBL, or similar). Multi-site required or strongly preferred
* Proven staff trainer: you have written SOPs and can point to people who still follow them after you left the room
* Direct communicator. Travels Hattiesburg, the Coast, and Meridian without being asked twice

* Your last role was nurse manager, charge nurse, or clinical supervisor and operations meant “keeping the floor calm”
* You describe your strength as patient rapport, bedside manner, or being the face of the office
* You need the physician or a vendor to fix EMR, claims, or report problems
* You have never written a workflow or trained a team to a documented standard
* You want a CEO title and strategy meetings more than you want queues, denials, and SOPs

* Live EMR or analogous systems exercise. If you cannot navigate a practice system, the process ends

* 90-day scorecard will be written into the offer: SOPs live at all three sites, staff competency documented, A/R and denial movement, owner time out of daily firefighting. Miss the build, and the seat does not continue.

How to apply

Email a résumé and a one-page note with exactly four items : (1) EMR/RCM/IT systems you configured yourself, (2) sites and headcount you ran, (3) one workflow you built and the metric that moved, (4) how you train staff when they do not follow the process. Advertising Copy

The Opportunity

The University of Vermont (UVM) invites nominations and applications for the position of Executive Director of Institutional Research and Assessment. Reporting to the Provost, the Executive Director will provide enterprise-level leadership for the Office of Institutional Research and Assessment (OIRA), advancing a strategic data, assessment, and decision-support agenda that strengthens institutional effectiveness, informs executive decision-making, and supports the University’s mission. This leader will foster a culture of responsible, transparent, and actionable data use; align data governance, analytics, assessment, and emerging technologies with institutional goals; and serve as a trusted advisor on the interpretation and strategic application of institutional data. The next Executive Director will also help define OIRA’s future role as both a steward of UVM’s official institutional data and a strategic partner with leaders across the University.

OIRA is responsible for the use and reporting of the University’s official institutional data and statistics regarding students, faculty, and staff, including accreditation, IPEDS reporting, and college ranking data, to name a few. The next Executive Director will provide institutional leadership, in partnership with Enterprise Technology Services, for data governance, stewardship, and architecture to ensure secure, accurate, reliable, and accessible data that supports regulatory reporting, contractual obligations, external requirements, institutional accountability, and lifecycle management practices that ensure data is collected, maintained, used, and retained in ways that are purposeful, efficient, and sustainable. They will work to advance an enterprise business intelligence and analytics strategy, including institutional metrics, dashboards, and self-service capabilities, while building campus-wide capacity for data- informed decision-making, data literacy, privacy and security, and the responsible and ethical use of advanced analytics and artificial intelligence, and lead adoption of these tools and practices across units to ensure consistent and effective use.

UVM is composed of nine schools and colleges, including the nationally recognized Larner College of Medicine, and offers a broad array of undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs. UVM enrolls approximately 14,000 students, including undergraduate, graduate, and medical students, across a variety of teaching modalities, and is supported by more than 4,000 faculty and staff. The University of Vermont is a public land-grant R1 research university, and is consistently recognized for its leadership in sustainability, inclusive excellence, and student

engagement, and has been ranked among the nation’s top public universities for making an impact. The schools and colleges offer over 100 bachelor’s degrees and more than 120 graduate degrees and certificate programs. To learn more about UVM, please visit: https://www.uvm.edu/

Priorities and Expectations for Leadership

Providing Support and Direction to a Strong Team

The OIRA office has a team of analysts and assessment professionals who are deeply committed to meeting the needs of the University. The next Executive Director will have the opportunity to build on this strong foundation by clarifying priorities, strengthening internal alignment, developing a sustainable service model, and positioning the team as a responsive, trusted, and strategic partner to academic and administrative units across UVM. In partnership with colleagues from Enterprise Technology Services, the Executive Director will also provide leadership for the data governance and data stewardship structures of UVM.

Providing Institutional Data and Analytics to Undergird the Implementation of the New Strategic Plan

As President Tromp establishes the University’s strategic direction through the finalization of the new strategic plan, Green, Gold, and Bold
, there will be strong interest from many stakeholders across the institution in OIRA’s support for data-identification and analysis of data sets at a variety of levels. The identification, definition and tracking of institution-wide metrics of achievement, and the distribution across the institution of responsibilities for achieving these metrics will be a first priority. OIRA will also support individual units, both in identifying and tracking their contributions to the institution-wide metrics outlined in the strategic plan, and for metrics specific to their divisional and unit goals. In this work, the Executive Director will have the opportunity to work closely with a variety of leaders across the campus in defining measures, identifying data sources, and then providing regular and timely reporting on the progress toward strategic objectives.

Support for Accreditation Analysis and Reporting

As a large public land-grant research university with an affiliated major medical center, UVM has significant institutional, programmatic, accreditation, financial aid, IPEDS, ranking, and external reporting obligations. The different programs, schools and colleges look to OIRA to assist with identification of key data needed for accrediting purposes, as well as retrieving, analyzing, and formatting the data elements to meet accreditation requirements. While OIRA has a strong reputation for excellence in this work, the new Executive Director will have the opportunity to further enhance the office’s approach, and where appropriate, formalize and standardize processes to support accreditation reporting across the institution.

Using Key Institutional Data to Provide Future Projections of Key Policy Areas and Make Policy Recommendations

As institutional data becomes increasingly integrated throughout the institution, and the use of AI becomes ever more ubiquitous, the need for sophisticated analysis and the ability for university leadership to utilize the analysis quickly and effectively becomes even more important.
